First, we recall the difference formula for cosine:

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(u-v)=\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v+\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

Applying the difference formula for cosine with $u=x$ and $v={60}^{∘}$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-{60}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡{60}^{∘}+\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡{60}^{∘} \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot \frac{1}{2}+\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\frac{1}{2}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$
